title_prefix: A wallet database that cannot be opened
mechanism: load-wallet (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1236) calls wallet-db-open (src/wallet/wallet-store.lisp:416-421) and then %load-wallet-records -> wallet-db-records (:429-445) without translating their conditions. Both signal bl.err:storage-error (BITCOIN-LISP.CONDITIONS:STORAGE-ERROR), which is not a subtype of bl.rpc:rpc-error, so handle-single-request's generic ERROR branch (src/rpc/server.lisp:407-420) turns it into +rpc-internal-error+ (-32603) with the message "Internal error: ~A" -- the raw LevelDB condition report. The wallet-error mapping that surrounds it works: the same handler answers -18 with Core's exact wording when the path does not exist (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1232-1235), so this is one unconverted condition class, not a missing mapping. Core routes every database failure through a DatabaseStatus: MakeDatabase sets FAILED_NOT_FOUND / FAILED_BAD_FORMAT for an absent or unrecognized file (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1329-1382), MakeSQLiteDatabase sets FAILED_VERIFY / FAILED_LOAD for a file it cannot open or verify (sqlite.cpp:697-703), and LoadWalletInternal sets FAILED_LOAD when LoadExisting returns nullptr, including for DBErrors::CORRUPT whose message is "Error loading %s: Wallet corrupted" (wallet.cpp:288-304, 2388-2390). HandleWalletError (rpc/util.cpp:127-157) then maps NOT_FOUND/BAD_FORMAT/LEGACY_DISABLED to RPC_WALLET_NOT_FOUND (-18), ALREADY_LOADED to -35, ALREADY_EXISTS to -36, NEW_UNNAMED/INVALID_BACKUP_FILE to -8, FAILED_ENCRYPT to -15, and everything else -- FAILED_LOAD and FAILED_VERIFY included -- to RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4). No Core path can answer a wallet-load request with -32603; protocol.h:34 reserves RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR for "genuine errors in bitcoind".
consequence: A wallet whose database is present but unreadable reaches the client as a JSON-RPC internal error carrying an implementation string ("LevelDB error: Corruption: CURRENT file does not end with newline"). Tooling and Core's own test suite switch on -18 (wallet missing / not a wallet) versus -4 (wallet error), and get neither; a -32603 conventionally reads as a node defect rather than a bad wallet, so an operator is pointed at the wrong thing. Nothing is mis-loaded -- wallet-db-records deliberately signals rather than returning a short record list -- so this is a diagnostic-class divergence, S3.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-wallet-s3, warm container image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4; probe build/ga11probe/p2.lisp (bitcoin-lisp.tests::ga11-p2), regtest wallet manager from tests/support/wallet.lisp. Wrote <wallets>/junk/CURRENT containing "garbage" (wallet-db-exists-p -> T, so the not-found branch is not taken), then: dispatch-rpc-method "loadwallet" ("junk") -> (:COND BITCOIN-LISP.CONDITIONS:STORAGE-ERROR "LevelDB error: Corruption: CURRENT file does not end with newline"), and the same call through bl.rpc::handle-single-request -> reply error object (-32603 . "Internal error: LevelDB error: Corruption: CURRENT file does not end with newline"). Controls in the same run: a name with no directory -> (:RPC -18 "Wallet file verification failed. Failed to load database path '.../wallets/nosuch/'. Path does not exist."), and an existing but empty directory -> the same -18 (Core answers -18 there too, with "Data is not in recognized format." -- wallet_multiwallet.py:305). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/util.cpp:127-157 (HandleWalletError), wallet.cpp:275-305 (LoadWalletInternal), wallet.cpp:2388-2390 ("Error loading %s: Wallet corrupted"), walletdb.cpp:1329-1382, sqlite.cpp:691-707, rpc/protocol.h:36/71/80. Functional tests: no wallet_*.py corrupts a descriptor wallet database and asserts a code, but the neighbouring load failures are asserted as -18 (wallet_multiwallet.py:295, :305; wallet_backup.py:100-101; wallet_crosschain.py:43-46) and -4 (wallet_multiwallet.py:300; wallet_backwards_compatibility.py:317), so a corrupt-database run would be the only Core wallet-load failure ever reported outside the -18/-4 pair.
fix_shape: Give the wallet-load path Core's DatabaseStatus classification instead of letting storage conditions escape. Wrap the wallet-db-open and wallet-db-records calls in load-wallet (and the same pair in restore-wallet and create-wallet) in a handler that catches bl.err:storage-error and re-signals bl.rpc:rpc-error, choosing the code the way HandleWalletError does: +rpc-wallet-not-found+ (-18) for the cases Core calls FAILED_NOT_FOUND / FAILED_BAD_FORMAT -- a missing directory, or a directory whose contents are not a recognized wallet database -- and +rpc-wallet-error+ (-4) with Core's "Wallet loading failed. Error loading <file>: Wallet corrupted" wording for a database that exists in our format but cannot be opened or scanned. Keep the underlying condition's text in the debug log (Core logs e.what() and puts only the classified sentence in the RPC reply) so the LevelDB string is still diagnosable without shipping it to the client, and add a regression test that opens a wallet directory with a deliberately damaged CURRENT and asserts the code, since the current shape passes any test that only checks that loadwallet fails.
